User.title: User
User.description: Represents a user of the SecureHub application.

id.description: Unique identifier for the User entity.

photoURL.description: URL of the user's profile photo.

createdAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the user account was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the user account was last updated.

UserProfile.title: UserProfile
UserProfile.description: Stores the profile information for a user.

id.description: Unique identifier for the UserProfile entity.

level.description: The user's current level in the security quiz.

totalXP.description: The user's total XP points earned.

totalBadges.description: The number of badges the user has earned.

passwordsChecked.description: The number of passwords the user has checked.

emailsChecked.description: The number of emails the user has checked for breaches.

quizzesCompleted.description: The number of quizzes the user has completed.

QuizResult.title: QuizResult
QuizResult.description: Stores the results of a single quiz attempt by a user.

id.description: Unique identifier for the QuizResult entity.

score.description: The user's score on the quiz.

completedAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the quiz was completed.

Quiz.title: Quiz
Quiz.description: Represents a quiz in the security learning platform.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Quiz entity.

Question.title: Question
Question.description: Represents a question in a quiz.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Question entity.

correctOptionId.description: Reference to Option that is correct. (Relationship: Question 1:1 Option)

Option.title: Option
Option.description: Represents an option for a question in a quiz.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Option entity.

PasswordCheck.title: PasswordCheck
PasswordCheck.description: Stores information about a password check performed by a user.

id.description: Unique identifier for the PasswordCheck entity.

passwordHash.description: A hash of the password that was checked. Note: Never store the actual password.

strengthScore.description: The strength score of the password.

breachStatus.description: The breach status of the password (e.g., 'Safe', 'At Risk').

checkedAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the password was checked.

MonitoredEmail.title: MonitoredEmail
MonitoredEmail.description: Stores information about an email address being monitored for breaches.

id.description: Unique identifier for the MonitoredEmail entity.

breachStatus.description: The breach status of the email address (e.g., 'Safe', 'At Risk').

lastCheckedAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the email address was last checked for breaches.

monitoringEnabled.description: A boolean indicating whether monitoring is enabled for this email address.

Badge.title: Badge
Badge.description: Represents a badge a user can earn in the application.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Badge entity.

description.description: A description of the badge and how to earn it.

UserBadge.title: UserBadge
UserBadge.description: Represents the badges earned by a user.

id.description: Unique identifier for the UserBadge entity.

earnedAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the badge was earned.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore data structure for SecureHub is designed with a focus on security, scalability, and ease of querying, adhering to the principles of Authorization Independence, Structural Segregation, Access Modeling, and Data Clarity. Each user's data is primarily stored under their own user ID, ensuring that security rules can be applied based on `request.auth.uid` without the need for complex `get()` calls. This design facilitates secure `list` operations (QAPs) and maintains integrity of ownership and timestamps.

**Authorization Independence and Denormalization:**

*   User-specific data (UserProfile, QuizResults, PasswordChecks, MonitoredEmails, UserBadges) are stored as subcollections under `/users/{userId}`. This ensures authorization rules can be based on path, i.e., `request.auth.uid == userId`.
*   No `get()` calls are required in security rules, enabling atomic operations and easier debugging.

**Structural Segregation:**

*   User-specific data is segregated from other users' data, ensuring that each user can only access their own information.
*   Global data like Quizzes, Questions, and Badges are stored in separate collections (`/quizzes`, `/questions`, `/badges`) without hierarchical authorization dependencies, simplifying management and access control.

**Access Modeling:**

*   **Private Data:** Path-based ownership is used for user-specific data (`/users/{userId}/...`).
*   **Collaborative Data:** Not applicable, as there is no collaborative data in this application.
*   **Global Roles (DBAC):** Not applicable, as there are no global roles in this application.

**QAPs (Rules Are Not Filters):**

*   The structure supports secure `list` operations because all documents within a collection share the same security requirements. For instance, listing quiz results under `/users/{userId}/quizResults` is secure because only the authenticated user can access their own quiz results.
